cards.text: Psalm 91 doesn't name its writer, but he opens with a promise: whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty. Shelter AND shadow, friend! My last shelter was a junk drawer, and my only shadow was a takeout menu.

cards.question: Then the psalm writer speaks for himself, straight to the LORD. What does he call Him?

cards.text: Then he turns to you, the listener: surely God will deliver you from the snare of the fowler and from the deadly plague. A trap AND a plague? That's a ROUGH week, friend, and the psalm says God gets you out of both.

cards.question: The psalm keeps going with a bird picture. How will God cover you?
Wings first, then something sturdier. The psalm calls God's faithfulness a shield.

cards.text: Next the psalm lists things you won't have to fear, starting with the terror of the night. Friend, I spent YEARS in a dark drawer, so the night and I have history.

cards.question: The only thing the psalm says you won't fear is what comes at night.

cards.text: Right, the list keeps going: the arrow that flies by day, the pestilence that stalks in the darkness, the calamity that destroys at noon. Night shift, day shift, LUNCH BREAK, the psalm's got every one of them on the schedule.

cards.question: Night, day, darkness and noon all show up in the list of things you won't fear. What's the big picture?

answers.text: There's no hour you need to fear

cards.text: Then the numbers get big. A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand.

cards.question: With a thousand falling at your side and ten thousand at your right hand, the psalm says no harm will come near you.
Thousands are falling, but not you. The psalm says you will only see it with your eyes and witness the ___ of the wicked.

cards.text: More big promises: no evil will befall you, no plague will approach your tent. And this time, the psalm tells you why.

cards.question: The psalm says no evil will befall you. What reason does it give?

answers.text: You have made the LORD your dwelling
You have never done anything wrong
You live far away from any danger

cards.question: Then the psalm says God sends help. He will command His ___ concerning you to guard you in all your ways.

cards.text: They will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone. Me? I stub my gold base on the oven door EVERY morning, so I'll take all the lifting I can get.

Heads up: the devil quotes these very lines to Jesus, tempting Him to throw Himself down from the top of the temple. Jesus answers with more Scripture: do not put the Lord your God to the test (Matthew 4:5-7).

cards.question: Lions and cobras usually mean danger. What does the psalm say you'll do to them?

cards.text: Then the voice changes. Now the LORD Himself is speaking about the one who stays close to Him, and I'd take my hat off, but then I'd just be a mustache on a base.

cards.question: The LORD says He will deliver this person. Why?

answers.text: Because he is stronger than others

cards.text: The LORD keeps going: when this person calls out to Him, He will answer. No hold music, friend. No 'your call is important to us.'

cards.question: The LORD promises the one who loves Him will never face trouble.

cards.text: He doesn't promise no trouble. He promises He'll be WITH him in it, and then He'll deliver him and honor him.

cards.question: The LORD's last promise: with long ___ I will satisfy him and show him My ___.
